findings.passage: He is back in the news because of what he has done since. On September 16, 2026, after a closed-door briefing for members of Congress organized by Sen. [Bernie Sanders](/personality-analysis/bernie-sanders), he told reporters lawmakers had "Maybe a year, but not much more than a year" to act on AI before it got away from them
findings.problem: The orientation paragraph explains why the article exists with a news-cycle status ('He is back in the news'). It will go stale within months, and the reader then gets a countdown quote ('Maybe a year') that expires on about 2027-09-16 (C61's own trigger). The thesis does not need it. 'Cannot leave a wrong alone' rests on 2012–2025 evidence: the Times correction, the Google exit, the Nobel promise, the OpenAI brief and the 2024–2025 'duty' statements. That makes the 2026 briefing one dated instance of a pattern, but the prose presents it as the reason to care. In 2031 the first thing a reader meets after the hook will be a lapsed deadline framed as current news.
findings.acceptance_test: Remove 'He is back in the news' and 'what he has done since'. Recast the 2026 briefing as a dated example of continued advocacy that began with his October 2024 'spend my time advocating' remark (for example, 'Since then he has turned that warning into a second career. On September 16, 2026, …'). Read with the September 2026 sentence deleted, the orientation paragraph still says who he is and why his choices matter. The 'Maybe a year' quote keeps its absolute date, and C61/C87 keep dated review triggers.

findings.passage: and in his late seventies he is briefing lawmakers
findings.problem: FAQ 'Why isn't Geoffrey Hinton a Type 5?' answers in the present tense with a temporary status ('in his late seventies he is briefing lawmakers instead of retiring'). FAQ text gets pulled into search snippets and structured data on its own, with no surrounding dates. That makes this the place where it will look out of date first, and become wrong once he stops or turns 80 (December 2027). The body's version ('He gave up retirement to brief lawmakers at 78') is dated and fine.
findings.acceptance_test: The FAQ uses dated past tense tied to the record, for example 'and since 2023 he has spent what was meant to be retirement warning the public and, in September 2026, members of Congress.' No FAQ answer uses the present tense for a changing activity, age bracket or role.

findings.passage: On his island, the contractors' mistakes still make him angry.
findings.problem: This is the last item in the discriminator ('It does not explain the heat'). It turns one 2023 reporter's observation ('still enrage him today', New Yorker, November 2023) into a timeless present-tense fact in the author's voice. The diagnosis paragraph does the same ('contractors' mistakes that still enrage him'). In five years 'still' will claim something nobody has checked, and the sentence carries type-argument weight.
findings.acceptance_test: Both author-voice instances are dated to the source, for example 'Years after the work was done, the contractors' mistakes still enraged him when the New Yorker visited in 2023.' The quoted 'still enrage him today' stays inside quotation marks, attributed to Rothman.

findings.passage: He does change his mind when the facts change. In 2023 he declined to sign a petition for a six-month pause in AI research ("China's not going to stop developing it for six months," he told the New Yorker). In October 2024 he said, "I've never recommended slowing the advancement of AI because I don't think that's feasible." By September 16, 2026, after the briefing on Capitol Hill, he was telling reporters: "It is going to get out of control unless we do something. We need to slow down."
findings.problem: The only example of a change in this paragraph is the most recent event. The 2023 and 2024 quotes say the same thing, so a single post-briefing remark to reporters carries the claim that he 'does change his mind.' C33's own alternative notes it 'may be rhetorical rather than a formal policy shift.' If the 2026 remark is later contradicted, clarified or superseded, the topic sentence loses its support. The article already has durable evidence of updating: backprop over the Boltzmann Machine, and the 2016 radiology prediction he called wrong in 2024.
findings.acceptance_test: The topic sentence rests on at least one non-recent example (backprop or radiology), or it is qualified so the 2026 line reads as an apparent shift ('appeared to move', 'told reporters'), not a settled reversal. C33 gets a dated review trigger (for example, by 2027-09-16, alongside C61).

findings.passage: In December 2024 he backed a legal brief opposing OpenAI's move away from nonprofit control.
findings.problem: The brief is correctly dated. But the record ends in December 2024, and C25's review trigger ('Re-check if OpenAI's corporate structure changes again') is written as if nothing has happened since. OpenAI's structure plan changed publicly after the brief: in May 2025 it announced the nonprofit would keep control, and a restructuring followed later that year. The evidence record (accuracy_checked_at 2026-11-04) has no dated source for any of it. That is a trigger already met and not processed. A reader in five years will reasonably ask whether the promise he defended was kept, and the closing section leans on this episode ('should not be torn up "when it becomes inconvenient"').
findings.acceptance_test: The evidence record contains an opened, dated primary or reliable source on what happened to OpenAI's nonprofit-control plan after December 2024, and C25's review trigger reflects that state. If the outcome is added to the body, it is one dated clause and does not imply Hinton's brief caused it. If it is left out, the body describes only the December 2024 position (as now), and the evidence record says why the outcome is omitted.

findings.passage: His partner, the retired sociologist Rosemary Gartner, said of him: "I think he's the kind of person who always needs a partner."
findings.problem: A current relationship is stated as a present-tense fact ('His partner') with no date, and C30 is marked stable. The standard lists relationships among the changing facts that need time_sensitive tracking and a review trigger. The quote comes from 2023 reporting.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence dates the relationship to its source (for example, 'His partner, the retired sociologist Rosemary Gartner, told the New Yorker in 2023…'). C30 is reclassified as time_sensitive with a concrete review trigger.

findings.passage: His own figure was that 20 percent of Indigenous communities in Ontario lack it.
findings.problem: A changing public-policy statistic is in the present tense ('lack it') and tracked as stable in C82. It is attributed and sits inside the December 2024 interview context, so it is not wrong now. But the figure will change, and the present tense makes it read as current.
findings.acceptance_test: The prose ties the figure to its date ('lacked it' or 'in 2024'). C82 is marked time_sensitive with a review trigger, or the sentence is reworded so it no longer reads as a current statistic.

protected_passages.passage: And just near the door there was a slightly smaller box that simply said, 'Not insects,' and that's where he had all the things about the family.
protected_passages.reason: A permanent, specific, self-reported detail that sets up the family pressure without a speculative childhood wound. It will mean the same thing in 2031.

protected_passages.passage: Masking tape along a closet shelf: "Do not prime shelf, prime shelf support."
protected_passages.reason: Concrete behavior far from AI. It is the most distinctive evidence for the 'correction' pattern, and it does not depend on any news cycle.

protected_passages.passage: Telling the story, he added: "I should've just moved the microwave upstairs."
protected_passages.reason: Tenderness and self-correction in one line. Unforgettable, sourced and timeless.

protected_passages.passage: It was a promise two young researchers made about a prize neither had any reason to expect, kept forty years later when keeping it cost real money.
protected_passages.reason: The most durable piece of the thesis. It rests on a fixed 1980s agreement and a December 2024 act, and it survives whatever happens in AI policy.

protected_passages.passage: It is for the next person who looks, to everyone else in the room, the way he did for decades: wrong, and sure of it.
protected_passages.reason: The ending comes back to the portrait instead of the news. It ties the prize to his career-long pattern and will not date.

assessment: Five-year test: the thesis mostly passes. Delete everything after 2025 and 'when Hinton decides something is wrong, he cannot leave it alone' still stands on dated, fixed evidence. That evidence is the May 2023 Times correction, the 2023 Google exit and his 2025 account of it, the 1980s Sejnowski agreement kept in December 2024, the December 2024 OpenAI brief, and the 2023 island observations. The hook (May 1, 2023) and the ending (the Sejnowski prize) are both durable. Ages check against the 1947-12-06 birth date (75 in spring 2023, 76 in October 2024, 78 in September 2026). Most events carry absolute dates. The weak points are a few present-tense status claims. The orientation paragraph's 'He is back in the news' plus an expiring 'Maybe a year' countdown is the most consequential (future-01). After that come the present-tense FAQ, the timeless 'still' anger, an undated partner relationship and a present-tense statistic. One topic sentence ('He does change his mind') rests only on the newest remark. One review trigger (C25, OpenAI structure) has already been met by post-2024 events that the evidence record does not mention. All are cheap to fix and none threatens the type argument. Tracking: C61/C87 have a dated trigger (2027-09-16). C33 and C25 have conditional triggers only, and C30/C82 should become time_sensitive. Similarity advisory: both tripped pairs (0.224 Aaron Pierre, 0.132 Daniela Amodei) match on body-triad vocabulary ('three types organized around anger'). That is ordinary type language, not reused argument. The surrounding paragraph moves straight to Hinton-specific evidence, and no other pair is above the 0.04 threshold, so there is no reuse finding. Scope note: this role did not reopen sources for quotation fidelity. It judged durability from the frozen draft and evidence record, plus general knowledge that OpenAI's structure plan changed publicly in 2025 (future-05 asks for a dated source rather than taking that on trust).
